title: Sen. Jeanne Shaheen’s daughter Stefany wins nasty primary for New Hampshire House seat
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A Democratic dynasty appears to be taking shape in New Hampshire.

Stefany Shaheen, whose mother Jeanne is retiring from the US Senate after three terms, edged out Marine veteran and former state Democratic Party Vice Chair Maura Sullivan in a bruising congressional primary on Tuesday.

With 91% of the estimated vote in early Wednesday, Shaheen led Sullivan, 37.3% to 35.0%, a margin of around 1,700 votes out of more than 75,000 ballots cast. Progressive Hampton selectwoman Carleigh Beriont finished in a competitive third place with 21.9% support.

Shaheen, a former Portsmouth city councillor, and Sullivan were vying to replace Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH), who gave up his seat for the chance to replace Jeanne Shaheen in the upper chamber.

The elder Shaheen has dominated New Hampshire Democratic politics for three decades, having been first elected governor in 1996, serving three terms, then becoming a senator in 2008.

The 79-year-old had actively courted donors and worked to help her daughter in the primary for the Granite State’s 1st Congressional District, which includes Stefany’s hometown of Portsmouth as well as the state’s largest city, Manchester.

A whopping $740,000 — 39% of the total donations the younger Shaheen’s campaign received — came from funders who previously made contributions to her mother, Politico reported.

Stefany Shaheen cited her experience on both the Portsmouth council and the city’s police commission as evidence that she could represent the state on her own merits rather than her last name.

Stefany Shaheen tried to cast herself as the most progressive of the primary candidates, even publicly splitting with her mother’s decision to back a deal to end a government shutdown last year. Her mother’s Senate colleague, Maggie Hassan, and Pappas’ predecessor in the House, Carol Shea-Porter, also endorsed the Shaheen campaign in a key last-minute boost.

Speaking to her supporters Tuesday night before the race was called, Shaheen said she was campaigning to “take on Donald Trump and his disastrous corruption, his endless war, his attacks on small business with these disastrous tariffs, the skyrocketing costs families are facing in New Hampshire and across the country.”

“We can bring the real change that’s needed, starting with healthcare, starting with Medicare for all,” she added.

Sullivan, whose allies took to the airwaves with an ad mocking Shaheen for her “fancy last name,” was endorsed by New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, and liberal groups like VoteVets and the Democratic Majority for Israel.

“What we are doing right now is send such an incredible message for change, and that politics as usual is not, is not going to get us where we need to go,” Sullivan told supporters Tuesday evening before the race was called.

In the Republican primary, political novice Anthony DiLorenzo, who owns a chain of car dealerships and has been endorsed by President Trump, easily defeated three other candidates — including Hollie Noveletsky, a veteran and nurse practitioner who runs a steel fabrication company and ran for the same seat two years ago.

“Our campaign is about prosperity,” DiLorenzo told supporters. “I believe that Washington, DC, needs more pragmatic businesspeople.”

In New Hampshire’s 2nd Congressional District, incumbent Maggie Goodlander swept aside a primary challenge from Paige Beauchemin, a progressive state lawmaker and nurse. Lily Tang Williams, who was the nominee two years ago and was making her third attempt at the seat, won the Republican primary.

With Post wires
